title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from White Grapes and Their Places
objectives: Link each grape to its classic regions

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its classic region.
steps.explanation: Every grape has a place that set its benchmark.

steps.prompt: Which compounds give Sauvignon Blanc passion fruit aromas?
steps.explanation: Thiols give tropical notes; pyrazines give green ones.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are usually made without oak?
steps.explanation: Côte de Beaune Chardonnay is classically fermented and aged in oak.

steps.prompt: Sémillon's thin skins make it prone to noble rot.
steps.explanation: Yes. That's why it is the main grape of Sauternes.

steps.prompt: Pinot Grigio in Italy is usually light and crisp, while Pinot ____ in Alsace is richer.
steps.explanation: Same grape, Pinot Gris, with the French name linked to the richer style.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc change with climate and winemaking
Riesling and Chenin make every style from dry to sweet
Aromatic grapes like Gewürztraminer and Viognier need careful picking
Each grape has a benchmark region worth knowing
